title: Inline Fixes, Microcopy, and Hero Snapshot Assets for Failure Mitigations
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Produce a compact set of onboarding and quickstart visual assets focused on error mitigation patterns that guide users to immediate, actionable fixes without leaving the quickstart flow. Deliver a hero snapshot (960x540) for docs and marketing, three inline micro-screens for in-product quickhelp, and a set of annotated screenshots for the docs site. Emphasis: legible microcopy for rate limits, timeouts, and retry guidance; subtle affordances for retry/resume actions; and a small ruleset for when to escalate to support. Assets must be usable by engineering for localizing microcopy and by docs for static images and animated GIFs.
acceptance_criteria: Hero snapshot (960x540) exported in PNG and web-optimized WebP showing a consolidated error state flow and CTAs
Three inline micro-screens (card components) designed at 320x180 that render correctly in the quickstart modal and console help drawer
Annotated screenshot pack (5 images) with callouts for copy, CTA, and suggested telemetry links for engineering
Microcopy strings extracted into a single CSV with context keys for i18n and engineering consumption
Design review completed with PM and Eng; at least two rounds of feedback addressed
Assets uploaded to Drive + Figma file shared with design/pm/eng and linked in ticket
design_notes: Visual language follows compact error palette (amber-60 for warnings, red-50 for hard failures) to avoid alarm fatigue
Prefer verbs-first microcopy: 'Retry now', 'Resume session', 'Reduce batch size'
Use a single-line limit of 55 characters for hero snapshot headlines to maintain legibility at 960px
Include an unobtrusive secondary action for 'View logs' that opens console debugging panel
Fallback behavior: when rate-limit info is unavailable, show an estimated reset time with tooltip explaining approximation
Avoid technical jargon in quickstart; map detailed phrases to 'Learn more' doc links in annotated pack

i18n (Nadia Ivanov): 'Avoid colloquialisms. Use 'about a minute' instead of 'in ~1m' to reduce translation ambiguity.'
